newsitem.title: UK: Sears to sell or demerge shoe division-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Sears to sell or demerge shoe division-newspaper.

text.p: British stores group Sears Plc has decided either to sell or demerge its troubled shoe division -- its single biggest business -- in a bid to turn itself round, the Sunday Telegraph newspaper said.

The group was looking at a series of options to jettison the British Shoe Corporation, which the newspaper said was the largest footwear business in Britain with annual sales of 600 million pounds ($1 billion).

It said the options included a break-up followed by a series of disposals, a joint venture with another show business, taking the business off the balance sheet or a demerger. Directors were committed to finding a permanent solution by end-1997.
The company tried to ditch part of the shoe business last year but this was scuppered when the stores had to be taken back from retailer Facia after it collapsed in June 1996.
Last week the group said annual profits would fall below last year's levels and also reported disappointing Christmas trading, an announcement which sent its shares plunging.
